structured_output.question: Why did compiling the airbench96-style port's forward+backward with torch.compile (mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs', PyTorch 2.4) plus a foreach/fused SGD make the timed prepare+train run slower (12.07 s vs 9.43 s at 9 epochs) instead of faster, with accuracy unchanged? Specifically: is the extra ~2.6 s a fixed cost leaking into the timed region (Dynamo guard failures or recompiles when train/eval mode, requires_grad, BN buffers or new shapes change after build; autotuning or cuDNN benchmark redone on the first real step; lazy compilation of the backward), or a real per-step slowdown of Inductor-generated conv/BN/GELU kernels compared with eager cuDNN for small-resolution, channels_last fp16 CNNs? Which diagnostics (per-epoch timing, TORCH_LOGS recompiles, Dynamo cache stats) and which fixes (compiling only non-conv parts, mode='default', static shapes, dropping the ragged batch, CUDA graphs) recover the expected 10–20% speedup?
